title: Methods, Records, Classes, and Encapsulation
summary: Design typed methods and small domain models using parameters, return values, properties, constructors, records, exceptions, and invariants.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Methods, Records, Classes, and Encapsulation
Use compiler and runtime evidence to test the contract

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Methods declare input and output contracts. Use optional parameters sparingly and place them after required parameters. C# passes arguments by value unless `ref`, `out`, or `in` is explicit; reference-type values still identify shared objects. Records are useful for value-oriented data, while classes suit identity and encapsulated mutable behavior. Keep setters private when updates require validation. Constructors should establish valid state, and public methods must preserve it. Throw specific exceptions for violated programming contracts and use result-style handling for expected user mistakes.
